title: On the rational solutions of generalized Abel equations: the composition condition for all-nonlinear Abel equations (Proposition 3.13)
author: L.A. Calderón* and I. Ojeda
work: On the rational solutions of generalized Abel equations
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's composition condition for generalized Abel equations with all terms nonlinear, printed as Proposition 3.13 at source0.tex lines 378-384 and delivered with the paper's own complete proof (lines 386-410). The statement is a structural rigidity theorem: if an all-nonlinear generalized Abel equation has as many distinct nonconstant rational solutions in one proportionality class as its top exponent minus one, then every coefficient is forced into the shape c_i p^{n_i-2} p' for one polynomial p, and consequently the equation satisfies the composition condition with the composed polynomial p^d, which over the reals makes the origin a composition center on intervals where p^d returns to its value. The proof is the paper's own assembly over the retained displays: it writes the solutions as scaled reciprocals of one polynomial, forms the auxiliary polynomial whose roots are the scalars, reads off its leading and constant coefficients against the denominator reduction, compares coefficients at the exponents of the equation to obtain each coefficient, and then rewrites the result as a composition. This is research-level differential algebra and Newton-diagram analysis, not a qualifying-examination exercise; the unit is H2.
